transcript: I'm sitting outside on a fire escape here to review the Sondheim final musical Here We Are and I am almost completely speechless about it which is the highest compliment I can give a piece of theatre if I'm being honest really only one other piece of theatre has made me feel the way here we are made me felt and that's David Bowie's Lazarus and Lazarus and Here We Are have a lot in common in terms of theme and in terms of how and why they were created I'm also gonna get progressively wetter and shinier through this because it's drizzling outside as I make it but I like the aesthetic of being part of the city now first before I say anything else I wanna thank the team over at The Shed the house team did an amazing job in a bad situation last night last night about two minutes before curtain it was discovered that TodayTix had sold my seat to someone else as well and that person showed up and we both had a ticket for the same seat and house management expertly fixed it like a minute before showtime by putting both of us in a beautiful premium third row center seat wonderful job the shed terrible job TodayTix but thank you for messing up your business in my favor I also wanna say this I was in row - I was in seat 1 0 8 on the side if you are sitting on the side and seat 1 0 8 1 0 7 1 0 6 you're not gonna see any part of act 1 I mean no part of Act 1 you'll see absolutely nothing it should not be marked as partial view it should be marked as almost no view so if you have one of those seats I don't wanna freak you out but you may wanna consider trying to change your ticket now Onward to the show as I said last night I never thought I'd live in a reality where there are Sondheim lyrics with the words Bitcoin Mountain Dew and Tesla referring to Elon Musk's car I wanna add to that I also thought I would never live in a reality where there is a f00t f3t!sh character in a Stephen Sondheim avant garde musical but my god am I living my best life right now because I am pleased to tell you that that reality is here Here We Are  in my opinion is the best piece of theatre running in this country right now Stephen Sondheim on his way out found a way to redefine the art form of musical theatre which I consider him the Shakespeare of for like the fourth time in his career this musical probably has the most like similarities to Conpany if I had to pick sonically it sounds kind of like a mix between Company and Sunday in the Park with George but it is definitely a concept show somebody on my discord asked me to try to describe the plot there is absolutely no way to do that it would be like trying to describe the plot of Lost Highway to a second grader it is impossible to describe the plot to this show to any living person and I'm gonna spoil the show past this point if you do not want the show spoiled do not continue watching I would recommend going into the show knowing absolutely nothing which is how I went into the show so this the first act of the show is about a group of friends who are just trying to find a place to eat and they keep going to different restaurants that represent different types of avant garde film making and they keep finding no food until they get trapped in an embassy during the end of the world and can't leave and that's the easiest way I can describe a show that is not about plot that's kind of about characters but it's really about theme and that theme is both anti capitalist and very anti millennial ha ha one of the first notes I wrote in underlined was Sondheim hated millennials and as a millennial I don't think I can really blame him for that it's not our fault that we've done absolutely nothing we've done nothing as a generation our benchmark is our nothingness our legacy is our nothingness all the reformers are doing just incredible work but particularly Denis O’Hare on with Mister David Hyde (Pierce) oh David somebody in my discord mentioned that he is like a sniper he is literally like a precision marksman that is the best way to describe what he's doing he's doing so much with so little and he is nailing every moment with the most precision I've ever seen on a stage it's really incredible Tracie Bennett is also one of the best parts of the show but I thought she was a little bit under utilized but maybe using her a little less made the audience appreciate what she was doing even more because I adored every single moment that featured her I just wanted to quickly add my absolutely favourite part of the show was Tracie Bennett's big number where she is a server in this French deconstructionalist avant garde restaurant oh my god I cannot stop thinking about it I also cannot stop thinking about the dream sequence number which I'm not gonna say that much about it is as good as anything Sondheim has ever written like I said this is one of the most monumental pieces of theater I've ever seen I will continue to think about this until the day I leave for new words but I do wanna get into some small critiques in my opinion the show really has issues in the last 10 minutes when they escape the room the show should end in my opinion no less than three to five minutes after they escape that room and it feels like it drags on after that quickly address yes you can in my opinion I know that the creative team has said Sondheim did not want any songs in Act 2 but in my opinion you can tell where he left to go on new adventures and you can tell exactly where he stopped writing and there in a perfect world there should be a giant Loveland like sequence of 30 minutes of music like apparently Sondheim wanted to make for Act 2 but we don't live in that perfect world and it's no use speculating what could have been it's just is what it is that Act 2 is in the state that it's in Musically and we should just accept that what I love a big uh Loveland sequence what I love it to end with a Sunday moment from Sunday in the park with George of course but if I'm being honest I'm just lucky that we got what we got back to the finale at one point all of the all all the main characters turn out and face the audience and kind of tell what they've Learned but I thought it that was kind of corny and I thought that it undercut a lot of the themes of the show because it kind of redeemed and lionized characters that should not have been lionized this character is about rich yuppie New Yorkers like the top 1% and I was filled in an audience of rich yuppie New Yorkers like the top 1% and I do wonder if they knew that the jokes were on them because it felt like they were laughing at the references in the jokes and not laughing at what the jokes were critiquing and I personally thought the last five minutes are part of the last five minutes undermined a lot of those themes and really clogged up the ending of the show besides that this is pure theatrical Nirvana this is pure theatrical magic very rarely do I think a show is worth what producers are charging you should refinance your house to sit front row centre for this I will go to my grave thinking about this huge moment in musical theatre history that I got to witness Stephen Sondheim is the coolest dude to ever live and created the coolest art that will ever be created in the musical theatre up until the day he left to go on new adventures run walk crawl anything you need to do to get your booty in that show no I do not think it should come to Broadway I think it should transfer to London and I think it should be filmed not everything needs to come to Broadway this is a perfect little gym taking it to Broadway with Andrew Jackson- Will Bloody Bloody Andrew Jackson it's tail in my opinion no it is not delegitimize a musical for it to be off Broadway and not on Broadway some musicals work better off Broadway Little Shop of horrors anyone Stephen Sondheim you're the greatest man to ever live
